scene: A hotel receptionist bows deeply from the waist behind a marble desk, head lowered, one arm sweeping down toward a waiting guest. Her uniform is crisp and pale. A wide bright lobby behind her, morning light across polished stone.

A young traveller slaps both hands flat against his own chest, leaning back with his eyebrows raised high and his mouth open in an exaggerated question. A ripe mango rests in an outstretched hand before him. Golden market light, crates of fruit behind.

A customer drives his head down in one hard nod, his whole arm flung out to point at a tall glass of milky orange iced tea standing on the cart counter. Ice bucket, curling steam, sunlit street behind him.

A farmer swings a steel pail down onto the straw beneath a cow, arm extended, body low over a milking stool. The cow's head is thrown back, mouth wide. Cold blue dawn through the open shed door, a lamp hanging above.

A man kneels on a picnic blanket and slams his open palm down onto the grass right beside his own knee, arm locked straight, leaning his whole weight into that one spot. Park lawn, scattered trees, bright afternoon light.

A man in a waistcoat thumps the butt of his snooker cue against his own chest, chin lifted, shoulders thrown back, one eyebrow raised. Behind him a green baize table sits under a low hanging lamp, smoke drifting through the beam.

A cook swings a wok up and away from the flame, arm high, a whole fountain of noodles and beansprouts hanging in the air above it. Her stall burns bright behind her: gas flames, steam, strings of warm lamps.

A schoolboy in a crisp white uniform stands beside his wooden desk and spins a large globe with a sweep of his whole arm, head tilted back, grinning. Rows of empty desks, morning sun through louvred shutters, dust hanging in the light.

A stallholder drops banknotes one by one into a battered biscuit tin cradled in her lap, her hand raised mid-release, her eyes down on the tin. Coins stacked on the counter beside her, shutters half down, one bare bulb overhead.

A waitress spins on her heel and throws one open hand out toward the last diner at the table, eyebrows high, head tilted. Two other diners sit back with their meals already in front of them. Warm light, white cloth, glassware.

A traveller halts mid-stride on wet tarmac and throws both arms wide in an enormous shrug, shoulders up, head turned back over one shoulder. His wheeled case lies tipped beside him. Dusk, aircraft and apron lights beyond.

An aunt in an apron bends all the way down and opens both arms wide toward a small child in the kitchen doorway, her head nodding, her face warm. A pot steams on the stove behind her, worn tiles, soft afternoon light.

A customer brings a fistful of coins down onto a wooden counter with a flat open hand, arm straight, leaning hard over the stall. A tall glass of milky orange iced tea steams beside the coins. Sunlit street behind.

A householder leans out through a half-open front door and takes the weight of a large brown parcel in both arms, knees bent, body braced. A delivery van waits at the kerb, rain on the path, grey afternoon light.

A woman raises one hand in front of a plain pale wall and pinches her thumb and forefinger almost shut, squinting hard at the tiny gap between them, her whole face leaning in toward her fingers. Soft even light, nothing else in the frame.

A buyer in a linen suit thrusts a thick brick of banknotes above his head with both hands, arms locked straight, chin up. Behind him a gleaming saloon revolves slowly on a turntable under white spotlights, onlookers ringed along the rail.

A woman rises from her restaurant table, one hand on her heart and the other arm flung wide, head back and mouth open in full song. White tablecloths and turned heads around her, a waiter halted mid-step, warm chandelier light.

A man in a dinner jacket stands up among the seated tables and thrusts one arm straight above his head, his other hand pressed flat on his own chest, grinning broadly. A crowded wedding reception behind him: flowers, white cloths, turning guests.

An engineer rises from his console and lifts both arms above his head, curving them together into one large empty circle, fingertips touching. Dim mission control, glowing screens, a rocket climbing off its pad beyond the wide window in white exhaust.

A woman thrusts a pair of tongs snapped clean in half across a hardware counter at arm's length, both hands out, leaning forward over it. Racked tools rise floor to ceiling behind her under hard strip lighting.

A doorman plants his straight arm across the chest of the next man in the queue, palm flat, turning his head away to look past him down the line. A red lamp burns over the door, velvet rope, night street.

A boy bends right down over his wooden desk, nose almost touching it, shoulders hunched and both elbows splayed out. Every other desk in the classroom stands empty. A small lamp beside him, shuttered windows, blue dusk outside.

A decorator stretches up on his toes and presses a loaded brush flat against the wall, arm extended along a taut string line pinned across the bare room. Small paint marks follow the line. Ladder, dust sheets, open tin, flat daylight.

An electrician on a wooden stepladder stretches a handheld meter up toward a bare bulb hanging on its cable, arm fully extended, a single needle swung far across a plain round dial. Dim workshop below, his face lit warm from beneath.

A stylist reaches up with both arms and clamps yet another roller onto a head already piled absurdly high with dozens of coloured curlers. The seated client laughs beneath the pile. Salon mirrors framed in warm bulbs.

A small woman staggers backwards under an enormous wrapped bundle of vegetables clamped in both arms, knees buckling, leafy greens and one long carrot bursting out over her face. Market stalls and crates of produce behind her, bright morning sun.

A soot-blackened chimney sweep hauls himself upright on the very last chimney pot of a long terrace roof, one arm raising a bundle of brushes overhead, his crooked tie hanging loose at his throat. Rooftops recede behind him under a low orange sun.

A middle-aged man in a work shirt tips a spoonful of tea leaves into a dented steel flask held up in his other hand, standing at a small kitchen table. His lunch tin, coat and keys lie squared up beside him. Grey dawn light.

A man thrusts one arm straight up above the heads of a crowded bar, a single finger extended high, grinning broadly with his lips pulled wide. Bottles glow behind the counter, shoulders press close around him, low night light.

A flamenco dancer in a red ruffled dress drives her heel down onto the tiles mid-stamp, back arched, one arm curved high above her head. A sunlit whitewashed courtyard behind her, a wooden chair, a guitar leaning against it.

A barefoot child skids to a stop in a bare schoolyard, both arms flung out and mouth open shouting, a thick golden cloud of dust boiling up around his feet. Other children run blurred behind him. A wall, a mango tree, hard sunlight.

An enormous glossy rooster struts down the centre of a village lane, chest thrown out, tail high, one foot lifted mid-step. A dog and two hens have stepped aside onto the verge. Wooden houses, mist between them, low golden light.

A village elder sitting on a low stool beside a cooking fire throws both arms wide, shaping something enormous in the air, mouth open mid-speech. Children and adults sit in a close ring around him, faces lit orange. Night, sparks rising.

A large brown rat sitting upright in an ornate carved chair on a raised dais lifts one forepaw, tail curled over the armrest. Below the dais two rows of officials in dark suits bow toward it. Marble columns, tiered benches, cold light.

A yellow robot arm swings a plain sealed box down onto a wooden pallet already stacked shoulder-high with identical boxes. The assembly line runs away behind it, a forklift waiting to one side with its forks raised. Hard factory light.

A masked nurse in a green gown thrusts a steel tray forward at full arm's length, a single clamp laid on it turned handle first. A bright overhead lamp throws a hard circle of light around her; everything beyond falls into shadow.
